Ben — thanks, Tue 02/17 11:00 PST works for us. Answers inline below.

> Peak inference throughput target (qps / tokens per second) and average request size.
We expect a peak of ~180 qps (inference requests), average request ~1.4k tokens. Bursty window ~10% of day.

> Egress restriction for metrics
We need metrics to remain within our VPC for now (security policy). We'll accept periodic push to an on-prem metrics aggregator or an IP-restricted endpoint.

> Firewall constraints (ports / mTLS / static IPs)
We require mTLS for control plane channels and will only allow egress to a small set of destination IPs (team will provide CIDR block).

I've uploaded a slightly updated diagram with an annotation about our metrics aggregator and a brief constraints sheet to the shared folder. Also attached the kickoff questions.

See you Tue.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deploy kickoff + initial diagram (Nimbus)

Thanks for the numbers, Samira — that helps. A few technical notes ahead of the readout so we can be concrete on the call:

1) Control plane connectivity model
- Our recommended pattern for private deployments is a one-way mTLS channel initiated by customer-hosted agents to Redwood's control plane over a restricted egress path. Control signals are small (config, versioning, rollouts).
- For customers that disallow any outbound to SaaS, we support a private control plane proxy deployed in their environment (VPC-hosted control plane) — that is a separate Private offering (note costs/ops).

2) Data plane attachment and segregation
- Model serving nodes should be placed in isolated subnets (we recommend 2 AZs minimum). Use separate subnets for model inference, caching, and telemetry to enforce ACLs.
- We'll publish a suggested CIDR allocation in the shared Drive doc. Traffic between customer app and model serving will stay within the customer VPC (no hairpin to Redwood hosted infra) when using Private deployment.

3) Metrics and telemetry
- Since Nimbus requires metrics inside the VPC, our agent can push to your metrics aggregator via an internal IP egress (customer-managed). We'll sign the mTLS cert for the agent -> aggregator channel.

4) Canary & fallback plan (short)
- Canary: start with 5% traffic to Redwood model variant inside a single AZ for 48 hours; monitor latency and correctness via eval prompts.
- Fallback: immediate rollback to on-prem replica + automatic DNS failover (pre-provisioned). We recommend pre-provisioned routing and low TTL for fast cutover.

5) Ops checklist we will bring to readout
- ACL/CIDRs for control plane egress (customer to provide)
- Certs/mTLS: CSR + CA pinning guidance
- Observability: token-level sampling, traces forwarded internally
- Runbook owner: assign a primary and secondary for 24/7 cutover window

I attached a short annotated diagram (runbook-diff-20260216.md) with recommended VLAN/subnet ranges and routing notes. We'll finalize these during the call.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-diff-20260216.md

Subject: Nimbus readout — decisions and next steps

Team — quick internal summary following the readout with Nimbus (call 02/17 11:00 PST):

Decisions made
- Control plane: Nimbus will allow outbound mTLS to a small set of Redwood control endpoints. They will provide CIDRs and static egress IPs by EOD 02/19.
- Data plane: Deploy Private model serving inside Nimbus VPC. Two AZs min, separate subnets for inference and telemetry.
- Metrics: Will remain in-customer. Redwood agent will push to their aggregator over mTLS.
- Canary: 5% traffic / 48h in single AZ, monitoring for latency regressions and quality drift.

Action items / owners
- Nimbus: provide CIDR block + firewall rules (owner: Samira) — due 2026-02-19
- Aditya: publish suggested CIDR allocations and VLAN plan to shared Drive (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1nimbus-private-vpc) — due 2026-02-18
- Irene: prepare egress ACL template + cert exchange playbook — due 2026-02-18
- Lauren: create the rollout Jira (INFRA-742) and link runbook — done (see Jira link).
- Ben: schedule 1st cutover window (proposed 2026-03-02 02:00-06:00 UTC) and coordinate on-call coverage.

Attachments pushed to shared folder: nimbus-private-deploy-diagram-v1.pdf, runbook-diff-20260216.md

I'll mark this thread as the canonical handoff for Nimbus Private deployment. If anything changes on CIDR/cert timelines let us know.
